subject: Oobah Butler
title: Who is Oobah Butler? The prankster behind HBO's new scam series
answer: Oobah Butler is an English filmmaker and writer known for stunts that expose how easily online systems can be gamed, most famously turning a fake restaurant, The Shed at Dulwich, into London's No. 1 on TripAdvisor in 2017. His five-part HBO docu-comedy, "Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow," premieres Nov. 22, 2026.
body:
Butler, born in 1992, started writing for Vice in 2015 and later made short films for the outlet. He became widely known in 2017 with The Shed at Dulwich, a restaurant that existed only as a listing and a garden shed in south London. Using fake reviews and clever photos, he pushed it to the top of TripAdvisor's London rankings, a stunt meant to show how little online ratings can be trusted. He later wrote a book about the experience, published in 2019.

He has since made several documentaries for Britain's Channel 4, including "The Great Amazon Heist" (2023), in which he tested how easily products can be listed and sold on the platform, and "How I Made £1 Million in 90 Days" (2025).

The new show, "Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow," is a five-episode HBO Original from A24, Abso Lutely Productions and Central, the company of filmmakers Josh Safdie and Ronald Bronstein. Daniel Lucchesi directs. According to HBO, Butler takes aim at industries and institutions including wine, wellness and royalty, gaming online reviews, inventing personas and launching fake companies to see how far he can get inside. The premiere airs Sunday, Nov. 22, at 11 p.m. ET/PT on HBO and streams on HBO Max; in Australia it arrives Nov. 23.

Viewers often ask whether his stunts are real. His past projects were documented, real-world pranks with verifiable results, such as the TripAdvisor ranking; the HBO series is billed as a docu-comedy, so expect real schemes presented with comic framing.
in_the_news: HBO premieres "Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow" on Nov. 22, 2026.
